source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 4 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
summary: Omar travels from N'Djamena into the Chadian savanna to stay with Wodaabe/Fulani herders during their Gerewol-style gathering, where painted, ornamented men dance and the women choose the most attractive man. The film opens on its most spectacular images (painted faces shot low and wide, Omar already in costume) and a personal childhood-memory voiceover, before resetting to a piece-to-camera in the capital at 1:19. A long, very dark night drive and camp (2:18-3:47) gives way to a drone dawn reveal and a slow village-immersion middle built on subtitled conversations and bead and make-up detail inserts. The second half escalates through Omar's own face painting (16:18-16:57) and joining the dance line (17:27-22:04) to the judging climax, then closes with a top-down drone of the dance circle that matches the 1:09 shot and a black logo card.
hook_analysis: Short visual lead-in followed immediately by speech (first speech 4.95 s). The first frames are the payoff images: low-angle wide-lens painted Wodaabe faces (0:00, 0:59) and a flash-forward of Omar wearing the headdress (0:10). Over these he gives a personal origin line about watching documentaries on African tribes as a child, illustrated by archival-looking footage inside a vintage TV frame (0:20). The stakes ('some people here had never seen someone with fair skin', 'To prove their masculinity', 'It's not about muscles') are posed as questions the film will answer. Replay heat is highest at 0:00-0:14, so the opening images are proven to work.
narrative_arc: Personal-memory hook -> capital arrival and briefing with guide (1:19-1:49, 'Six hours?!') -> night drive into the bush and camp (1:59-3:47) -> dawn reveal and first village contact (3:57-5:46) -> daily-life immersion: homes, cooking, teeth care, migration (5:56-10:00) -> preparation of the men: make-up ingredients, beads, dress (10:03-12:21) -> gathering and first dances (12:31-15:38) -> context map of Chad's neighbours (15:58) -> Omar is painted and dressed (16:18-17:27) -> full ceremony and judging (17:47-22:23) -> reflection and farewell (22:33-23:41) -> logo card.
camera_and_composition: Heavy use of a wide lens close to subjects, often from below, so painted faces fill the frame against sky (0:00, 0:59, 20:05). Medium two-shots of Omar with locals for conversation (5:56, 13:20), handheld following shots of Omar walking with guides (5:06, 9:23), detail inserts of feet, beads, phone and cooking (8:04, 10:12, 11:02, 15:48), and drones for scale and as section punctuation (1:09 top-down circle, 4:07-4:17 sunrise, 9:03, 14:19, 22:33, 23:23). Presenter close-ups of Omar thinking or reacting (5:16, 10:32, 13:10, 15:38). Exact camera moves and cuts are not observable at storyboard resolution.
color_and_grade: Warm-neutral daylight with muted, slightly lifted greens and teal-leaning skies (palette #61888b), moderate saturation (0.43) that lets the saturated costumes, pink turbans and beadwork carry the colour. The night section is genuinely underexposed (15% low-key frames), lit by fire and headlamps rather than brightened. Archival and map inserts get a distinct vintage, washed-out treatment inside a rounded TV frame.
sound_and_music: Speech coverage 0.605 at about 115 wpm: the film is talk-led but leaves gaps. The longest speech-free runs cluster in the ceremony half (12:35-13:03, 14:06-14:31, 14:36-15:07, 16:37-16:54, 17:43-18:22, 20:25-20:47), which suggests the dances play out on music or natural sound rather than narration. 49 questions in the transcript: Omar asks locals and also asks himself questions on camera. The audio itself was not analysed.
what_to_borrow: Open on the visual payoff (the costume/ritual faces and yourself already transformed) under a single personal 'why I came' line, then reset to the arrival
Let the night journey stay dark and long enough to feel remote; follow it with a drone dawn reveal
Build up the ritual through its ingredients (make-up powders, beads, clothing) before showing the ritual itself
Put the presenter through the transformation (painted face, costume, dancing) as the second-half climax
Bookend with a matching top-down drone of the central ritual (1:09 and 23:23)
what_to_avoid_copying: The fair-skin novelty line and 'beauty contest' framing can read as exoticising if the context is not given by the community itself
Mid-film subscribe animation (16:48) interrupts the build-up straight after the face painting
Several minutes of near-black night frames will not hold attention without strong audio

observations.name: payoff-image cold open
observations.description: Low-angle wide-lens painted Wodaabe faces against blue sky, then Omar already wearing the headdress among them (0:10), a flash-forward to the 17:27-20:54 dance. This is the highest replay-heat segment.

observations.name: childhood-memory framing over archive
observations.description: Personal VO about watching documentaries on African tribes as a child, illustrated by archival-looking footage inside a vintage CRT frame (0:20).

observations.name: top-down drone of dance circle
observations.description: Overhead drone of the dancers' ring with long shadows at 1:09; the same view returns at 23:23 to close the film.

observations.name: capital arrival piece-to-camera
observations.description: Omar in a car park ('Greetings from N'Djamena') at 1:19, then a subtitled exchange with the guide while the 4x4 is loaded (1:29-1:49); comic 'Six hours?!' reaction and a no-hotels reveal.

observations.name: dark night journey and camp
observations.description: Driving POV through the window (1:59-2:08), then near-black frames of a night drive, campfire, chairs and tea (2:18-3:47). The darkness is kept rather than brightened.

observations.name: dawn wake-up and drone reveal
observations.description: Omar peers out of a tent (3:57), cut to drone sunrise over savanna woodland with long shadows (4:07-4:17), then a piece-to-camera at camp (4:27-4:46).

observations.name: subtitled interviews with herders
observations.description: Omar with a man in a pink turban and a guide in white (5:56-6:05) and a woman cooking (6:15); Arabic subtitles are burned in at the bottom for local speech.

observations.name: village-life replay peak
observations.description: Second-highest replay segment: Omar walks through the camp among women and children (7:05-7:15) while the narration describes homes and cooking.

observations.name: ornament detail inserts
observations.description: Close-ups of beaded leg wraps (10:12) and striped beadwork (11:02) cut between wide-lens portraits of made-up men (10:22, 10:52, 11:31) as the make-up materials are explained.

observations.name: map graphic in vintage frame
observations.description: Satellite-style map with Chad flagged in its colours and Libya/Sudan labelled, inside the rounded vintage TV frame (15:58), as Omar asks about neighbouring countries.

observations.name: Omar is painted (participation)
observations.description: Make-up applied to Omar's face on a blue tarp (16:18-16:38), a subscribe-button animation at 16:48, then a frontal close-up portrait of his painted face (16:57) as a reveal.

observations.name: presenter joins the dance
observations.description: Omar in headdress waving and clapping among dancers (17:27-17:57), shot from below with the wide lens.

observations.name: ceremony climax
observations.description: Dense coverage of dancers' faces and lines (18:07-20:35), ending on the replay-peak close-up of a dancer with wide eyes and bared teeth (20:05), which fits the narration about eyes and teeth as beauty criteria.

observations.name: judging and Omar's pick
observations.description: Families watch while the judging happens ('Everyone chooses who they think is the man'); Omar dances arm-raised with the men (21:54-22:04) and announces 'My choice goes to...'.

observations.name: reflection, drone bookend and logo card
observations.description: Drone over the forest (22:33), portrait close-ups, the top-down dance-circle drone again (23:23), Omar walking alone (23:32), a closing greeting, then a black Omar Farooq logo card from 23:42.
